description: Comment scrubbing, LLM-tell detection, and the doc-comment discovery loop, which are easy to confuse with each other and with the per-language documentation standards.

queries.query: Scrub the useless comments out of internal/, the ones that just restate the code like `// increment i`.
An LLM wrote half of this codebase and the comments are full of 'This function elegantly handles...'. Clean them up.
Should this comment stay? `// Loop over users` above `for _, u := range users {`
Remove the banner comments and ASCII dividers from src/ and trim the comments that narrate what the code does.
Strip the comment slop from our Go and Rust code, but keep the comments that explain why.
Does this README read like ChatGPT wrote it? Score it paragraph by paragraph.
Check my conference talk script for AI-sounding phrasing and tell me which paragraphs to rewrite.
Our docs/ folder reads like slop: 'delve', 'robust', 'seamless' everywhere. Flag the worst paragraphs.
Is this paragraph AI-generated? "In today's fast-paced world, it's crucial to leverage robust solutions."
Find every exported function in this package that's missing a doc comment and add them, most important first.
Audit the doc-comment coverage of our public API, fix the gaps, then make sure it still compiles.
Half of our public Rust items have no docs. Find them and document them in priority order.
Which public classes in this Python package have missing or stub docstrings? Fix the important ones.
Our exported TypeScript functions have placeholder JSDoc like '@param x - the x'. Find the deficient ones and fix them.
Fix the typo in the README title.
Write a blog post announcing our new release.
Add a code comment explaining why we retry three times here.
Translate the README into Spanish.
Turn on the lint rule that requires comments on exported functions.
Summarize what this module does.
